body.notify: Extends Epic `complete-consistent-richer-code-index-one` (c2ba6fa6): adds a Story that makes the settle pass after file events proportional to the changed files, building on DEF-c2ba6fa6, Story s1's settle mode and pending-row index, and absorbing ISSUE-61045de91faef1a0; code in src/indexer/index.ts, src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts, src/indexer/external-endpoints.ts, src/indexer/messaging-endpoints.ts and src/db/entities.ts.

addedStory.title: Settling file changes does work proportional to the changed files, never a scan of the repository or the store
addedStory.userValue: After an edit, a branch switch or a merge, the graph catches up in time proportional to what changed: a burst of file events no longer costs one whole-repository resolve per file, and reading one file's or one repository's entities no longer passes over every other repository's rows. The results are the same as a full index gives.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository whose index is complete, and one file in it that changes
acceptanceCriteria.when: the settle pass for that file event runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the entity rows, pending rows and edges it reads are those the changed file defines, imports, exports or awaits, and their number does not grow with the size of the repository or of the store

acceptanceCriteria.given: a burst of file events touching N files of a repository
acceptanceCriteria.then: the work done grows with N and with what those files touch, not with N times the repository

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same file changes settled event by event, and the same files indexed by a full index
acceptanceCriteria.when: the edges and pending-row classes of those files are compared
the entities of one file, or of one repository, are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: no row of another file or another repository is read, and the result is what it is today

nextAction.description: Approve the HLD amendment (`AMD-c2ba6fa62a148ed1-8`) and the updated Epic, then run `design.story` for the new Story `s13` to produce its LLD.

feedback.author: Subho Ghosh (stakeholder, chat 2026-10-17)
feedback.comment:
Stakeholder decision, 2026-10-17 (chat): s13 is designed around a persistent unresolved-edge map, not dependency ordering.

Design: each file is parsed and stored as it arrives; every edge it cannot resolve is kept in a persistent map in the store keyed by what it awaits (repository, kind, name, or the awaited id). When a later file stores an entity, the map is looked up by that entity's name/id; each waiting edge is checked with the same visibility rule cross-file resolution uses (the caller imports the file, reaches it through a re-export, or for Go/JVM shares its package), resolved when exactly one visible candidate exists (ambiguous with candidates when several do), and removed from the map. Reverse direction: when a file is re-indexed or deleted, every resolved edge pointing into its entities goes back into the map instead of vanishing, and is re-resolved when the file's new entities are stored. No indexing order and no dependency discovery; applies to every supported language; language-specific gaps (Kotlin package mapping, JVM callee naming) stay with s12. Depth-first dependency ordering was considered and rejected: import cycles, import-less same-package dependencies and parse-only discoverable targets (Kotlin/Scala) make it unreliable.

Added acceptance criteria:

ac5 - Given file A calls a function that file B defines, and A is indexed before B; when B arrives through a file event; then A's call is an edge, as after a full index, with no repository scan.

ac6 - Given A's call to B's function is an edge; when B is edited (re-indexed) or deleted and re-created; then A's call is an edge again once B's new entities are stored, and while B's function does not exist the call is pending, never lost.

Evidence (experiments 2026-10-17 against the real parser and resolver over a temporary store): indexing a.ts (calls foo) before b.ts (defines foo) leaves foo with no callers after both settles and after a whole-repository pass; after a first index where foo's callers were [a], editing and re-indexing b.ts leaves foo with no callers, also after a whole-repository pass.
